title: Photoperiodic Flower Induction
objective: Describe flower induction as genotype-specific perception of recurring light-dark cycles and separate induction, visible flowering, and later development.

terms.definition: Physiological commitment toward reproductive development before flowers are necessarily visible.
Formation of reproductive meristem structures following induction.
Flowering promoted when day length is sufficiently short or the uninterrupted night sufficiently long.
Operational endpoint that must define the visible or anatomical criterion used.

coreScience: Photoperiod cannabis generally initiates reproductive development after repeated inductive cycles with sufficiently long nights. Leaves perceive light and transmit flowering signals to meristems. Visible pistillate structures occur after upstream signaling, so the timer switch date is not the same as the date of induction or the date of visible flower.

The threshold is not universally 12 hours. Controlled research across essential-oil, grain, and fiber hemp found cultivar-dependent critical responses and showed that small day-length changes could delay flowering in some genotypes. Seed lots sharing a name may also differ genetically.

Temperature, plant age, maturity, stress, light intensity, twilight, night interruption, spectrum, and prior photoperiod can modify response. Day-neutral germplasm follows a different developmental control pattern. Production records must therefore identify genotype, source, propagation history, and operational milestone.
cultivationRelevance: Accurate induction records support crop scheduling, stretch management, space planning, sex-expression scouting, and comparison of cultivars.
Changing photoperiod and intensity simultaneously alters both developmental signaling and photon dose; the two changes should be recorded separately.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Cultivar, source lot, clone or seed, photoperiod classification, and prior observed response.
Measured day length, night length, transitions, spectrum, twilight or leaks, and DLI.
Switch date, first preflower, first defined floral initiation sign, stretch interval, and full-flower criterion.
Age, node count, size, health, stress, training, and reproductive maturity at switch.
Day/night temperature, VPD, irrigation, root-zone status, CO2, and deviations.

misconceptions: The flip instantly creates flowers: Induction and meristem transition precede visible flower development.
Twelve hours is the natural threshold for all cannabis: It is a common conservative schedule; critical response varies by genotype and conditions.
More darkness always means faster or better flowering: Excess dark time reduces daily photons and may not improve developmental or yield outcomes.
evidenceLimits: Published critical photoperiods are specific to tested germplasm and endpoints. They cannot authenticate a cultivar name or predict every indoor drug-type response.
